title: Hologram Projection Shader Between GLB Objects
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that loads two GLB models — OrientationTest.glb and DirectionalLight.glb — and implements a hologram projection system where OrientationTest.glb acts as the 'projector' (Object A) and DirectionalLight.glb acts as the 'receiver' (Object B). The hologram shader projects a scanline-based holographic effect onto Object B based on the relative position and orientation of Object A.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 8) looking at origin.
- Add OrbitControls for camera manipulation.
- Dark background color #0a0a1a to emphasize the hologram glow.
- Add a subtle ambient light (intensity 0.15) and one dim directional light (intensity 0.3) so the base geometry is barely visible without the hologram.
- Load OrientationTest.glb (Object A / Projector) and place it at (-3, 1, 0). Scale uniformly to 1.5.
- Load DirectionalLight.glb (Object B / Receiver) and place it at (3, 1, 0). Scale uniformly to 1.5.
- Draw a thin cyan line (THREE.Line with dashed material) connecting the centers of Object A and Object B to represent the projection beam.

HOLOGRAM SHADER (applied to Object B's materials):
- Create a custom ShaderMaterial that replaces Object B's default materials.
- Uniforms: uTime (float, animated), uProjectorPos (vec3, world position of Object A), uHoloColor (vec3, default cyan 0.0,1.0,0.9), uIntensity (float, 0.0-2.0, default 1.0), uScanlineFreq (float, default 80.0), uScanlineSpeed (float, default 2.0), uActive (bool, default true), uDistanceFalloff (float, computed from distance between A and B), uFlickerAmount (float, 0.0-1.0, default 0.15), uEdgeGlow (float, 0.0-1.0, default 0.6).
- Vertex shader: pass worldPosition, worldNormal, and vUv to fragment. Compute fresnel factor from view direction and normal.
- Fragment shader: (1) Compute scanlines using sin(worldPosition.y * uScanlineFreq + uTime * uScanlineSpeed) mapped to 0.3-1.0 range. (2) Compute distance attenuation: 1.0 / (1.0 + uDistanceFalloff * dist * 0.1) where dist is distance from fragment to projector. (3) Compute directional factor: dot product of normalized (projectorPos - fragPos) with fragment normal, clamped 0-1. (4) Compute flicker: 1.0 - uFlickerAmount * fract(sin(uTime * 43.23) * 12.34). (5) Compute edge glow using fresnel: pow(1.0 - abs(dot(viewDir, normal)), 2.0) * uEdgeGlow. (6) Final color = uHoloColor * scanline * attenuation * directional * flicker * uIntensity + edgeGlow * uHoloColor. Alpha = (scanline * attenuation * directional * 0.7 + edgeGlow * 0.3) * uIntensity. Use transparent blending, AdditiveBlending, depthWrite false.

INTERACTIONS:
1. DRAG Object A: Implement raycasting-based drag on Object A. When user clicks and drags Object A, it moves on the XZ plane (Y stays at 1). The projection beam line updates, uProjectorPos uniform updates, and the hologram on Object B changes in real-time (distance falloff and directional factor change).
2. KEYBOARD CONTROLS:
   - 'H' key: Toggle hologram on/off (uActive). When off, Object B shows a dim grey wireframe instead.
   - 'I' / 'K' keys: Increase / Decrease uIntensity by 0.1, clamped [0.0, 2.0].
   - 'F' / 'G' keys: Increase / Decrease uScanlineFreq by 10.0, clamped [10.0, 200.0].
   - 'R' key: Reset all shader parameters to defaults AND reset Object A position to (-3,1,0).
   - 'C' key: Cycle hologram color through: cyan(0,1,0.9) -> magenta(1,0,0.8) -> green(0,1,0.3) -> cyan. Track colorIndex 0,1,2.
   - 'U' key: Undo last parameter change (maintain a history stack of up to 20 states). Each state stores {intensity, scanlineFreq, colorIndex, projectorPos, active, flickerAmount}.
   - 'Y' key: Redo (if undo was used and no new change made since).
3. DOM CONTROLS: Add a HUD panel (top-right, semi-transparent dark background, 220px wide) with:
   - A range slider for uFlickerAmount (0.0 to 1.0, step 0.05, default 0.15), labeled 'Flicker'.
   - A range slider for uEdgeGlow (0.0 to 1.0, step 0.05, default 0.6), labeled 'Edge Glow'.
   - A checkbox labeled 'Wireframe Overlay' that toggles a wireframe overlay on Object B (add a second wireframe mesh on top).
   - A text display showing current distance between A and B, updated live.
   - A text display showing current FPS.

STATE MANAGEMENT — expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame:
{
  modelsLoaded: boolean (true when both GLBs loaded),
  projectorPos: {x, y, z} (Object A world position, 2 decimal places),
  receiverPos: {x, y, z} (Object B world position),
  distance: number (Euclidean distance A-to-B, 2 decimals),
  holoActive: boolean,
  intensity: number (2 decimals),
  scanlineFreq: number,
  colorIndex: number (0=cyan,1=magenta,2=green),
  currentColor: {r, g, b} (current holo color components),
  flickerAmount: number (2 decimals),
  edgeGlow: number (2 decimals),
  wireframeOverlay: boolean,
  undoStackSize: number,
  redoStackSize: number,
  isDragging: boolean,
  elapsedTime: number (shader uTime, 1 decimal),
  fps: number (integer),
  beamVisible: boolean (whether the connecting line is rendered),
  projectorUniformSynced: boolean (true if uProjectorPos matches Object A actual position within epsilon 0.01)
}

ANIMATION: In the render loop, update uTime with elapsed seconds, update uProjectorPos from Object A's world position, update uDistanceFalloff, update the beam line geometry endpoints, update all __3D_STATE__ fields, and update HUD text displays.

Make sure both models are fully loaded before enabling interactions. Show a loading indicator until ready.
physics_constraints: Distance falloff must follow inverse-distance law. Hologram intensity must remain clamped [0.0, 2.0]. Scanline frequency clamped [10.0, 200.0]. Flicker and edge glow clamped [0.0, 1.0]. Undo/redo stack must maintain full consistency — redo stack clears on any new action. Projector uniform must always be synced with Object A mesh position within epsilon 0.01. Color cycling must be deterministic and wrap correctly. All numerical state values must be NaN-free at all times.
